    HOW TO PLAY
    
    
    
      
    
        
    DRIVE
    
        
      
          
    • WGas
      • 
          
    • SReverse
      • 
          
    • SpaceBrake (X too)
      • 
          
    • ADSteer
      • 
          
    • ShiftHold to drift: the car gets less grip, so it slides more easily
      • 
          
    • QEGear down / up (G manual on/off)
      • 
        
    
      
    
      
    
        
    TOUCH SCREEN
    
        
      
          
    • PedalsGas and Brake on the right. Drift is the same as holding Shift: the car lets go of the road more easily. Rev is reverse.
      • 
          
    • ButtonsTwo arrows steer left and right.
      • 
          
    • WheelPut a finger on the wheel and turn it. It springs back to straight when you let go.
      • 
          
    • TiltHold the phone like a steering wheel and turn it. Tap Centre if the car pulls to one side. The first time, your phone may ask to allow motion sensors.
      • 
          
    • Change itTap the STEER button on the screen, or Settings › Controls. Nothing zooms when you tap twice, so you can mash the pedals.
      • 
        
    
      
    
      
    
        
    GAME
    
        
      
          
    • RBack on the road
      • 
          
    • YMain menu: change car, play solo, or find a lobby
      • 
          
    • ←→In the garage: change car. The filters narrow the list and HEAR IT plays the engine
      • 
          
    • FFlash lights + horn: slower cars ahead move over. In a police car: lights and siren
      • 
          
    • CCamera · Z handbrake
      • 
          
    • OSettings (scenery, camera, sound). Dev mode, in solo play only, adds the tuning, traffic and road menus
      • 
          
    • PPause · U units · M mute · K hide HUD
      • 
        
    
      
    
      
    
        
    AIDS, CAMERA, HUD, ONLINE
    
        
      
          
    • NHSteering assist on / off (the car counter-steers for you)
      • 
          
    • LTraction control: off, lite, full
      • 
          
    • Right-dragLook around the car: 360° in chase, head look in cockpit. Scroll zooms
      • 
          
    • `Adjust camera height, distance and field of view
      • 
          
    • JMove, resize or hide the gauges, score, crash card and map
      • 
          
    • VMap of the whole loop: zones, tunnels, bridges, rest area, landmarks and where everyone is
      • 
          
    • ILobby window: players and chat (only inside a multiplayer lobby: host or join one from the main menu)
      • 
          
    • TEnterChat with the others in your lobby (Esc leaves the text box)
      • 
        
    
      
    
      
    
        
    SCORING
    
        
      
          
    • StartGo over  to start a run. Stay under it for  and the run is banked.
      • 
          
    • Near missPass a car within . Close (under ) pays ×2, very close (under ) ×3. The faster you go, the more it pays.
      • 
          
    • BonusesOncoming car ×1.5 · big rig ×1.25 · threading between two cars ×2 · sideswipe · drifting over 40 km/h.
      • 
          
    • ComboEvery pass raises the multiplier (up to ×). It drains if nothing happens for .
      • 
          
    • CrashA hard hit on traffic or a wall ends the run. Its points still count towards your best and your wallet.
      • 
        
    
      
    
      
    
        
    MONEY, CARS AND UPGRADES
    
        
      
          
    • EarnEvery point you score pays , crashes included. While the police chase you each point pays .
      • 
          
    • CarsOpen the menu (Y) and flick through the garage. Every car has its own price; you can look at any car but only drive one you own.
      • 
          
    • UpgradesOwned cars take engines, turbos, tyres, brakes, suspension and more. Each costs money.
      • 
          
    • Dev modeSettings › Developer, solo only: everything is free and the tuning menus unlock, but nothing is earned or saved.
      • 
        
    
      
    
      
    
        
    POLICE CHASE (SOLO)
    
        
      
          
    • ChaseStay over  for a few seconds and  police cars come after you. They are tuned to the maximum, quicker than you, weave through the traffic without hitting it and never get left behind: if you gain on them they come back on the road round you. The traffic pulls over for them.
      • 
          
    • HeatEvery  seconds the heat goes up (to ): more cars (up to ), faster and braver ones.
      • 
          
    • TacticsPIT: a car pulls up on your rear quarter and turns into it, hard enough to spin you. Box: cars hold both sides and squeeze. Block: one runs ahead, takes your lane and brakes. Once you are shut in on every side the box brakes together until you stop, and the cars holding you do not get shoved out of the way. The HUD says BLOCKED, BOXED IN or CORNERED.
      • 
          
    • BustedStop or crash with them around you and it is over: your time and stats, then Play again or Home. Leaving the road does not shake them: they follow you down the ramp and into the gas-station lot.
      • 
          
    • Who chasesQuick cars (over  top speed) are chased mostly by the sport police cars (Mustang Pursuit, 911 GT3 RS), with a few Lamborghinis and Roadsters among them. Slower cars get the Crown Vic and the SUV first, and the sport police cars join in as the chase goes on.
      • 
          
    • Normal or ChasePick Chase on the solo set-up page (or in Settings) to have police; Normal has none. Lobbies never have police.
      • 
        
    
      
    
      
    
        
    READING THE TRAFFIC
    
        
      
          
    • BlinkerThat car is about to change lane. It checks the gap first.
      • 
          
    • Brake lightsIt is slowing down. Back off or pick another lane.
      • 
          
    • HazardsIt is wrecked and drifting to a stop.
      • 
          
    • MinimapBlue cars go your way, orange cars come at you, red are wrecks. Flashing red and blue dots are police, green dots are other drivers, and the line ahead follows your lane. Tap it, or press V, for the whole loop.
      •
